item.caption:
From Washington City to Logan, Utahns showed up Saturday for the fourth nationwide “No Kings” day of protests — but this time, participants voted, too.

The demonstrations were meant to mobilize people to cast their midterm ballots early ahead of Election Day on Nov. 3, organizers said.

In Salt Lake City, protesters marched from the Capitol to a ballot drop box by Salt Lake City’s Main Library.

Around two thousand people gathered at the Capitol ahead of the march, filling the steps with American flags, protest signs, music and costumes — and a recurring message that change starts at the ballot box. Many in the crowd had already voted, but some who brought their ballots proudly waved them in the air.

🔗: Read more at the link in our bio.

(✍️: Samantha Moilanen | 📹: @LandwehrPhotography)

Sunday Blessings 

Vision & Victory! 
Stepping Into Early Voting & Election Day! 
Tomorrow marks the start of early voting! Over the coming days and through Election Day, my amazing team and I will be out on the front lines, serving our community and working hard.
As we embark on this crucial stretch, I am placing everything in God’s hands and praying for:
Health & Physical Strength to keep our energy high and stay safe through long days.
 Direction & Wisdom to make sound decisions, lead well, and handle every situation with grace and clarity.
Victory for the vision, purpose, and future we are fighting so hard for.
Thank you to everyone who has supported, prayed for, and stood by us throughout this journey. Your encouragement means the world!
If you are heading out to vote during early voting or on Election Day, make your voice heard! Let’s finish this strong together. 🗳️
